title: sparse-span-forwarder-conditional-compression-async-ack
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our OTLP ingest tier sees large numbers of sparse spans (short-lived, high-cardinality service-to-service traces) that blow up downstream backing stores (Tempo and external vendors) and increase egress costs. Existing exporters either forward everything (causing noise and cost) or aggressively drop spans (losing fidelity for debugging).

Goal: Build a forwarding component that conditionally compresses span bundles and provides an async-ack surface for downstream exporters to reduce peak load and cost while retaining trace fidelity for debug-worthy flows. This work focuses on the OTLP-to-Tempo/Jaeger path and should be compatible with external vendor exporters.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 40% reduction in tokens/bytes sent to Tempo during sparse-span bursts without increasing end-to-end ingest latency > 50ms median.
- No more than 2% increase in trace-loss for spans marked as "critical" by sampling rules.
- Exporter error rate (5xx from Tempo or vendor) reduced by 60% during previous burst patterns.

Design approach:
1) Detection: implement a burst detector in the span-router that identifies sparse-span bursts using sliding-window unique-span-key cardinality + service-pair heuristics.
2) Bundling & conditional compression: when a burst is detected, instead of sending many small span envelopes, the forwarder builds compressed bundles using a light dedupe + delta-encoding scheme (configurable per-tenant). Compression mode has three levels: none, gzip, and delta+snappy.
3) Async-Ack API: introduce a lightweight async-ack handshake between the forwarder and exporters (Tempo adapter / vendor exporters). The forwarder returns an immediate ACK to ingress after writing to a local durable queue; downstream delivery is retried internally with backoff. This reduces tail latency seen by clients while providing durability guarantees.
4) Circuit-breaker & fallback: if the exporter signals sustained 5xx or queue backlog exceeds threshold, the forwarder will switch to a preserve-critical-only mode (send only spans matched by sampling label/priority) and emit telemetry.

Operational controls:
- Tenant-level toggles: compression_level, async_ack_enabled, burst_sensitivity, preserve_critical_threshold.
- Runtime metrics: compressed_bytes_sent, uncompressed_bytes_dropped, bundles_created, exporter_retry_count, queue_backlog_seconds.
- Dashboards: new "Sparse Span Forwarder" dashboard with per-tenant heatmap, bundle size distribution, exporter latency P50/P95/P99, and burst detector firing rate.

Compatibility and integration notes:
- The async-ack is a best-effort opt-in protocol. Legacy exporters that do not support async-ack will be upgraded via adapter shim that provides the durability queue.
- Must preserve trace ids and parent-child relationships when bundling; preserve ordering for spans within a single trace.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for dedupe and delta encoding logic.
- Integration tests with a tempo-dev cluster to validate bundle unpacking and trace reconstruction.
- Chaos test: simulate sustained Tempo 503 responses to validate circuit-breaker fallback and no client-facing latency regressions.
- Load test scenario: replay historical sparse-span burst trace logs (from incident 2024-11-09) through staging to validate savings and correctness.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind tenant opt-in in staging.
2) Invite beta accounts (2 internal + 3 customers) for 2-week pilot.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% tenants -> 50% -> 100% across 2 weeks, with automated rollback on SLO breach (exporter 5xx > 1% or queue_backlog_seconds > 300).

Monitoring & alerting:
- Alerts: exporter_retry_count > 100/min (P0), queue_backlog_seconds > 120s (P0), compressed_bytes_sent increase > 200% (P1) for a tenant.
- Dashboard links and example queries will be attached in attachments.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Sparse+Span+Forwarder+Design
- Load test scripts: https://drive.redwood.ai/observability/load-tests/sparse-forwarder-replay.tar.gz
- Tempo staging cluster: https://tempo.staging.redwood.ai/ (internal)
